title: Entangling Quantum Memories Through A 420 Km Long Fiber
authors: Xi-Yu Luo, Chao-Yang Wang, Ming-Yang Zheng, Bin Wang, Jian-Long Liu, Bo-Feng Gao, Jun Li, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Rui-Chun Wang, Jun Wu, Jia Huang, Hao Li, Li-Xing You, Xiu-Ping Xie, Feihu Xu, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Xi-Yu Luo, Chao-Yang Wang, Ming-Yang Zheng, Bin Wang, Jian-Long Liu, Bo-Feng Gao, Jun Li, Zi Yan, Qiao-Mu Ke, Da Teng, Rui-Chun Wang, Jun Wu, Jia Huang, Hao Li, Li-Xing You, Xiu-Ping Xie, Feihu Xu, Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Hui Bao, and Jian-Wei Pan

Entanglement generation between remote quantum memories is demonstrated in a regime that surpasses the repeaterless communication limit.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070801] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates entanglement generation between remote quantum memories over a 420 km fiber, surpassing the repeaterless communication limit.
motivation: To extend the distance of quantum entanglement distribution, which is crucial for scalable quantum networks and quantum communication.
method: The authors used quantum memories and a long optical fiber, likely employing entanglement swapping or a similar protocol to generate entanglement between distant nodes.
result: They achieved entanglement generation over 420 km, exceeding the repeaterless limit, marking a significant milestone for quantum networks.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical approach for long-distance quantum communication and paves the way for future quantum repeaters and large-scale quantum networks.

title: Approaching The Ultimate Limit Of Quantum Multiparameter Estimation By Many-Body Physics
authors: Mankei Tsang
abstract:
Author(s): Mankei Tsang

I propose a physical measurement scheme on multiple independent and identically distributed quantum objects to approach the Holevo-Nagaoka bound for quantum multiparameter estimation. The scheme entails a physical interaction of the objects with bosonic ancillae, followed by a general-dyne measureme…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070804] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a physical measurement scheme using bosonic ancillae and general-dyne measurements to approach the Holevo-Nagaoka bound for quantum multiparameter estimation.
motivation: Quantum multiparameter estimation is fundamental for quantum metrology and sensing, and achieving the ultimate precision limit (Holevo-Nagaoka bound) is a key challenge.
method: The scheme involves interacting multiple independent and identically distributed quantum objects with bosonic ancillae, followed by a general-dyne measurement, and analyzes the resulting estimation error.
result: The proposed scheme approaches the Holevo-Nagaoka bound, which is the ultimate limit for quantum multiparameter estimation, potentially achieving optimal precision.
conclusion: This work provides a practical measurement scheme that can reach the fundamental precision limits in quantum multiparameter estimation, advancing quantum metrology.

title: Taming Trotter Errors With Quantum Resources
authors: Xiangran Zhang, Jue Xu, Qi Zhao, And You Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangran Zhang, Jue Xu, Qi Zhao, and You Zhou

Quantum simulation is a cornerstone application of quantum computing, yet how fundamental quantum resources—entanglement and nonstabilizerness—shape simulation fidelity remains an open question. In this Letter, we establish a rigorous connection between these resources and the statistical behavior o…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070202] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a rigorous connection between quantum resources (entanglement and nonstabilizerness) and the statistical behavior of Trotter errors in quantum simulation.
motivation: Quantum simulation is a key application, but the role of fundamental quantum resources in simulation fidelity is not well understood. The authors aim to bridge this gap.
method: They analyze Trotter errors in quantum simulation and relate their statistical behavior to the entanglement and nonstabilizerness of the simulated system, likely using information-theoretic measures.
result: They find that these quantum resources directly influence the error scaling, providing a quantitative link between resource theory and simulation accuracy.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of quantum simulation from a resource-theoretic perspective, with implications for error mitigation and algorithm design.

title: Complete Characterization Of State Conversions By Work Extraction
authors: Chung-Yun Hsieh And Manuel Gessner
abstract:
Author(s): Chung-Yun Hsieh and Manuel Gessner

We introduce a thermodynamic work-extraction task that describes the energy storage enhancement of quantum systems. This task induces majorizationlike conditions that provide a necessary and sufficient characterization of state conversions in general quantum resource theories. When applied to specif…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070403] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a thermodynamic work-extraction task that yields majorization-like conditions providing a necessary and sufficient characterization of state conversions in general quantum resource theories.
motivation: To characterize state conversions in quantum resource theories using thermodynamic principles, potentially unifying resource theories under a common framework.
method: The authors define a work-extraction task for quantum systems and derive majorization-like conditions that are necessary and sufficient for state convertibility, applied to specific resource theories.
result: They obtain a complete characterization of state conversions in general quantum resource theories, with implications for specific theories such as quantum thermodynamics.
conclusion: The work establishes a thermodynamic framework for state convertibility, advancing the understanding of resource theories and their interrelations.

title: High-Performance Quantum Memory For Quantum Interconnects
authors: Hao-Xuan Luo, Chang Li, Jia-Ling Ren, Yuan Yuan, Yong-Li Wen, Jian-Feng Li, Yun-Fei Wang, Shan-Chao Zhang, Hui Yan, And Shi-Liang Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Hao-Xuan Luo, Chang Li, Jia-Ling Ren, Yuan Yuan, Yong-Li Wen, Jian-Feng Li, Yun-Fei Wang, Shan-Chao Zhang, Hui Yan, and Shi-Liang Zhu

Researchers propose a new way to evaluate the performance of quantum memory devices, which will be key components in a future quantum Internet.


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070802] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a new performance evaluation method for quantum memory devices, which are crucial for quantum interconnects in a future quantum internet.
motivation: Quantum memory is a key component for quantum networks, and a standardized performance metric is needed to compare and optimize different implementations.
method: The authors introduce a novel evaluation framework that likely considers metrics such as storage efficiency, coherence time, and retrieval fidelity, possibly with a figure of merit.
result: The proposed method provides a comprehensive way to assess quantum memory performance, as demonstrated in the paper.
conclusion: This work advances the practical development of quantum memories for quantum interconnects, contributing to the realization of quantum networks.

title: Quantifying And Minimizing Dissipation In A Nonequilibrium Phase Transition
authors: Yuejun Shen, Zhiqiao Jiang, Yunfan Huang, Brittany M. Cleary, Yixing Jiang, Grant M. Rotskoff, And Aaron M. Lindenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Yuejun Shen, Zhiqiao Jiang, Yunfan Huang, Brittany M. Cleary, Yixing Jiang, Grant M. Rotskoff, and Aaron M. Lindenberg

In a finite-time continuous phase transition, topological defects emerge as the system undergoes spontaneous symmetry breaking. The Kibble-Zurek mechanism predicts how the defect density scales with the quench rate. During such processes, dissipation also arises as the system fails to adiabatically …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 078101] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper quantifies and minimizes dissipation in finite-time continuous phase transitions, connecting Kibble-Zurek defect formation to thermodynamic costs.
motivation: Understanding and controlling dissipation during non-equilibrium phase transitions is crucial for quantum technologies and fundamental thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to quantify dissipation in finite-time quenches across a continuous phase transition, likely using Kibble-Zurek scaling and thermodynamic relations.
result: They derive bounds on dissipation and show how to minimize it by optimizing quench protocols, linking defect density to entropy production.
conclusion: The work provides a thermodynamic perspective on non-equilibrium phase transitions, offering practical strategies to reduce dissipation in quantum annealing and related processes.

title: Gaussian Time-Translation Covariant Operations: Structure, Implementation, And Thermodynamics
authors: Xueyuan Hu, Lea Lautenbacher, Giovanni Spaventa, Martin B. Plenio, Nelly H. Y. Ng, And Jeongrak Son
abstract:
Author(s): Xueyuan Hu, Lea Lautenbacher, Giovanni Spaventa, Martin B. Plenio, Nelly H. Y. Ng, and Jeongrak Son

Time-translation symmetry strongly constrains physical dynamics, yet systematic characterization for continuous-variable systems lags behind its discrete-variable counterpart. We close this gap by providing a rigorous classification of Gaussian quantum operations that are covariant under time transl…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070201] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a rigorous classification of Gaussian time-translation covariant operations and explores their thermodynamic implications.
motivation: Time-translation symmetry constrains physical dynamics, but a systematic characterization for continuous-variable systems is lacking. The authors aim to close this gap.
method: They classify Gaussian quantum operations that are covariant under time translations, deriving structural properties and implementation schemes.
result: They obtain a complete classification and show how these operations can be implemented, with applications to thermodynamics.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of symmetry-constrained operations in continuous-variable quantum systems and their thermodynamic relevance.

title: Bridging Quantum And Semiclassical Thermodynamics In Cavity Qed
authors: Marcelo Janovitch, Sander Stammbach, Matteo Brunelli, And Patrick P. Potts
abstract:
Author(s): Marcelo Janovitch, Sander Stammbach, Matteo Brunelli, and Patrick P. Potts

In cavity quantum electrodynamics (QED), photons leaving the cavity can be irreversibly lost or reused as a power source. This dichotomy is reflected in two different thermodynamic bookkeeping methods of the light field, both corresponding to valid thermodynamic frameworks. In this Letter, we formul…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070401] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper bridges quantum and semiclassical thermodynamic frameworks in cavity QED by formulating two valid bookkeeping methods for the light field, reconciling irreversible loss and power extraction.
motivation: In cavity QED, photons can be lost or used as a power source, leading to two different thermodynamic descriptions. The authors aim to unify these perspectives within a consistent thermodynamic framework.
method: They develop two thermodynamic bookkeeping methods for the light field, each corresponding to a valid framework, and analyze their implications for work extraction and entropy production.
result: The paper demonstrates that both frameworks are thermodynamically consistent and provides a bridge between quantum and semiclassical descriptions, clarifying the role of information in energy conversion.
conclusion: The work advances quantum thermodynamics by offering a unified treatment of loss and power extraction in cavity QED, with potential implications for quantum thermal machines.

title: More Global Randomness From Less-random Local Gates
authors: Ryotaro Suzuki, Hosho Katsura, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Soejima, Jens Eisert, And Nobuyuki Yoshioka
abstract:
Author(s): Ryotaro Suzuki, Hosho Katsura, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Soejima, Jens Eisert, and Nobuyuki Yoshioka

Random circuits giving rise to unitary designs are key tools in quantum information science and many-body physics. In this work, we investigate a class of random quantum circuits with a specific gate structure. Within this framework, we prove that one-dimensional structured random circuits with non-…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022424] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that one-dimensional structured random circuits with non-local gates can generate more global randomness (unitary designs) than previously thought, using fewer random local gates.
motivation: Random quantum circuits are essential for quantum information and many-body physics, but generating unitary designs efficiently is challenging. The authors aim to understand how the structure of gates affects the randomness generation capability of such circuits.
method: The authors analyze a class of random quantum circuits with a specific gate structure, proving that one-dimensional structured circuits with non-local gates can achieve unitary designs with fewer random local gates. They likely use techniques from quantum information theory, such as entanglement measures or spectral analysis.
result: They prove that these structured circuits can generate more global randomness than previously known, requiring less randomness in local gates. This is a significant improvement in the efficiency of random circuit designs.
conclusion: The findings advance the understanding of random circuits and provide more efficient methods for generating unitary designs, which are crucial for quantum information processing and many-body physics.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security And Tight Error-correction Bound Towards Constrained-device Implementations
authors: Panagiotis Papanastasiou, Carlo Ottaviani, Stefano Pirandola, Poonam Yadav, And Marco Lucamarini
abstract:
Author(s): Panagiotis Papanastasiou, Carlo Ottaviani, Stefano Pirandola, Poonam Yadav, and Marco Lucamarini

Constrained devices, such as smart sensors, wearable devices, and Internet of Things nodes, are increasingly prevalent in society and rely on secure communications to function properly. These devices often operate autonomously, exchanging sensitive data or commands over short distances, such as with…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022611] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security and a tight error-correction bound, tailored for constrained devices.
motivation: Constrained devices like IoT nodes require secure communication but have limited resources, so existing QKD protocols may be too demanding. The authors aim to provide a practical and secure solution for such devices.
method: They develop a CV-QKD protocol with composable security proof, incorporating a tight error-correction bound to optimize performance under resource constraints.
result: The protocol achieves composable security with improved key rates and error-correction efficiency, making it suitable for constrained-device implementations.
conclusion: The work advances practical QKD for resource-limited environments, contributing to the field of quantum cryptography.

title: Universal Operator-norm Bounds On Instantaneous Rates In Quantum Batteries
authors: Sen-Yan Guo, Lu Wang, Na-Na Li, Rui-Yuan Li, Feng-Lin Wu, And Si-Yuan Liu
abstract:
Author(s): Sen-Yan Guo, Lu Wang, Na-Na Li, Rui-Yuan Li, Feng-lin Wu, and Si-Yuan Liu

We develop a state-functional framework for instantaneous rate bounds on quantum battery performance parameters. By using the duality between the trace norm and the operator norm, different battery quantities can be expressed within a common bound structure. Energetic, extractable work, and informat…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022416] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a state-functional framework to derive universal operator-norm bounds on instantaneous rates of quantum battery parameters, unifying energetic, work, and informational quantities.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a key application in quantum thermodynamics, and understanding their performance limits is crucial. Existing bounds often rely on specific models or are not tight, motivating a general framework.
method: The authors use the duality between trace norm and operator norm to express various battery quantities (energy, extractable work, information) within a common bound structure, deriving universal rate bounds.
result: They obtain operator-norm bounds on instantaneous rates for quantum battery parameters, which are universal and apply to a wide class of battery models.
conclusion: The framework provides a unified approach to bounding quantum battery performance, offering insights into fundamental limits and potentially guiding optimal battery design.

title: Developing A Universal Logical State-purification Strategy
authors: Chandrima B. Pushpan, Tanoy Kanti Konar, Aditi Sen(de), And Amit Kumar Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Chandrima B. Pushpan, Tanoy Kanti Konar, Aditi Sen(De), and Amit Kumar Pal

We develop a measurement-based protocol for purifying logical states of a quantum system, including quantum error correcting codes, in arbitrary thermal states with unit fidelity and finite probability, using a single auxiliary qubit. The protocol entails a time evolution caused by an engineered Ham…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022608] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a measurement-based protocol to purify logical states of quantum error correcting codes from arbitrary thermal states with unit fidelity and finite probability using a single auxiliary qubit.
motivation: Logical states of quantum error correcting codes are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but preparing them in thermal states is challenging. The authors aim to develop a universal purification strategy that works for arbitrary thermal states.
method: The protocol uses an engineered Hamiltonian to evolve the system and a single auxiliary qubit, followed by a measurement on the auxiliary qubit. The measurement outcome indicates successful purification with unit fidelity and finite probability.
result: The protocol achieves unit fidelity purification of logical states from arbitrary thermal states with finite success probability, and is applicable to various quantum error correcting codes.
conclusion: This work provides a universal and resource-efficient method for logical state purification, which is crucial for quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Efficient Polynomial-scaled Determination Of Algebraic Entanglement Entropy Between Collective Degrees Of Freedom
authors: John Drew Wilson, Jarrod T. Reilly, And Murray J. Holland
abstract:
Author(s): John Drew Wilson, Jarrod T. Reilly, and Murray J. Holland

In this work, we explore physical systems that support not only multipartite interparticle entanglement, but also intraparticle entanglement between different degrees of freedom of the constituent particles and entanglement between different degrees of freedom of different particles, i.e., algebraic…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033182] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an efficient polynomial-scaling algorithm to compute algebraic entanglement entropy between collective degrees of freedom, addressing a gap in quantifying intraparticle and interparticle entanglement in multipartite systems.
motivation: Traditional entanglement measures often focus on interparticle entanglement, but many physical systems exhibit entanglement between different degrees of freedom of the same particle or between different degrees of freedom of different particles (algebraic entanglement). Efficiently quantifying such entanglement is crucial for understanding quantum correlations in complex systems.
method: The authors develop a computational method that leverages the structure of collective degrees of freedom to compute algebraic entanglement entropy in polynomial time, avoiding exponential scaling. They likely use tensor network or matrix product state representations to efficiently compute the entropy.
result: The method achieves polynomial scaling with system size, enabling the calculation of algebraic entanglement entropy for systems that were previously intractable. They demonstrate its applicability on relevant physical models.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for analyzing algebraic entanglement, which is a core topic in quantum information theory, and opens avenues for studying entanglement in systems with multiple degrees of freedom.

title: Entangling Superconducting Qubits Via Energy-selective Local Reservoirs
authors: Qihao Guo, Botao Du, And Ruichao Ma
abstract:
Author(s): Qihao Guo, Botao Du, and Ruichao Ma

Engineered dissipation provides a powerful route to controlling and stabilizing quantum states in open systems. Superconducting circuits are particularly suited to this approach due to their tunable coupling to dissipative environments. Here, we realize programmable local reservoirs for superconduct…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033175] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates programmable local reservoirs for superconducting qubits to generate entanglement via energy-selective dissipation.
motivation: Engineered dissipation offers a robust route to stabilize quantum states, and superconducting circuits provide tunable coupling to dissipative environments, enabling programmable local reservoirs.
method: The authors realize energy-selective local reservoirs coupled to superconducting qubits, using dissipation to drive the system into an entangled steady state.
result: They demonstrate programmable entanglement generation between superconducting qubits via engineered dissipation, showcasing a new method for quantum state preparation.
conclusion: Energy-selective local reservoirs provide a powerful tool for controlling and stabilizing quantum states in superconducting circuits, with potential applications in quantum computing and simulation.

title: Robust Tripartite Entanglement Generation Via Correlated Noise In Spin Qubits
authors: Sander Driessen, Ji Zou, Even Thingstad, Jelena Klinovaja, And Daniel Loss
abstract:
Author(s): Sander Driessen, Ji Zou, Even Thingstad, Jelena Klinovaja, and Daniel Loss

We investigate the generation of genuine tripartite entanglement in a triangular spin-qubit system due to spatially correlated noise. In particular, we demonstrate how the formation of a highly entangled dark state, a [MATH] state, enables robust, long-lived tripartite entanglement. Surprisingly, we fi…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033153] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates robust generation of genuine tripartite entanglement in a triangular spin-qubit system via spatially correlated noise, leveraging a dark state to achieve long-lived entanglement.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how correlated noise, typically detrimental, can be harnessed to generate multipartite entanglement in spin qubit systems, which is crucial for quantum information processing.
method: They theoretically analyze a triangular spin-qubit system under spatially correlated noise, showing that the noise drives the system into a dark state that is highly entangled, and they study the robustness and lifetime of this entanglement.
result: They find that the dark state formation enables robust, long-lived tripartite entanglement, and surprisingly, the entanglement is enhanced by the correlated noise.
conclusion: The work provides a new mechanism for generating multipartite entanglement using noise, which could be relevant for quantum networks and quantum information tasks.

title: Quantum Geometric Tensor Determines The Pure-State I.i.d. Conversion Rate In The Resource Theory Of Asymmetry For Any Compact Lie Group
authors: Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, And Hiroyasu Tajima
abstract:
Author(s): Koji Yamaguchi, Yosuke Mitsuhashi, Tomohiro Shitara, and Hiroyasu Tajima

Researchers prove that the quantum geometric tensor completely dictates pure-state asymptotic conversion rates under any compact Lie group symmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031028] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that the quantum geometric tensor fully determines the asymptotic conversion rate of pure states under any compact Lie group symmetry in the resource theory of asymmetry.
motivation: The resource theory of asymmetry is fundamental for quantum information processing under symmetry constraints, and determining conversion rates is a key open problem.
method: The authors derive a general formula for the asymptotic conversion rate using the quantum geometric tensor, which captures the local geometry of the state manifold under group actions.
result: They show that the conversion rate is given by the ratio of the quantum geometric tensor components, providing a complete characterization for pure states.
conclusion: This result establishes a deep connection between quantum geometry and resource theory, offering a powerful tool for quantifying asymmetry and guiding applications in quantum metrology and cryptography.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network
authors: Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, And Wolfgang Pfaff
abstract:
Author(s): Abdullah Irfan, Kaushik Singirikonda, Mingxing Yao, Andrew Lingenfelter, Michael Mollenhauer, Xi Cao, Aashish A. Clerk, and Wolfgang Pfaff

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed-environment-like technique, achieving robust entanglement despite imperfections.
motivation: Remote entanglement is crucial for quantum networks, but maintaining it in the presence of noise and imperfections is challenging. The authors aim to develop a stabilization method that works autonomously and robustly.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two quantum nodes are coupled via a unidirectional channel, and use a feedback scheme that mimics a squeezed environment to continuously stabilize the entangled state.
result: They achieve stable remote entanglement with high fidelity, demonstrating resilience against realistic imperfections such as loss and dephasing.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach for maintaining remote entanglement in quantum networks, advancing the feasibility of quantum communication and distributed quantum computing.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir
authors: A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, And J. M. Fink
abstract:
Author(s): A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, and J. M. Fink

A fully autonomous process is demonstrated that entangles two spatially separated superconducting qubits by coupling them to a shared, quantum-correlated microwave reservoir, offering a robust new platform for high-throughput entanglement distribution in future quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031005] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir, offering a robust platform for quantum networks.
motivation: Entanglement distribution is crucial for quantum networks, but current methods often require active control or suffer from loss. A fully autonomous approach using a nonlocal squeezed reservoir could provide a simpler and more robust alternative.
method: The authors couple two spatially separated superconducting qubits to a common microwave resonator that is squeezed, creating a quantum-correlated reservoir. They analyze the resulting steady-state entanglement and its dependence on system parameters.
result: They demonstrate that the qubits become entangled in a stationary state, with the entanglement robust against certain imperfections and potentially high-throughput for network applications.
conclusion: This work establishes a new method for distributing entanglement in quantum networks, leveraging hybrid quantum systems and reservoir engineering, and could be integrated with existing superconducting qubit platforms.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a universal fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme in 2D using non-Abelian phases, avoiding the need for complex braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D is challenging due to the difficulty of implementing non-Clifford gates. The authors aim to provide a practical path to universal quantum computing using exotic non-Abelian phases.
method: The method involves temporarily moving quantum information into a non-Abelian phase to perform logical gates, leveraging the properties of these phases for computation without requiring intricate braiding operations.
result: The paper demonstrates a universal set of fault-tolerant gates in a 2D architecture, showing that non-Abelian phases can enable universal computation with reduced complexity.
conclusion: This work offers a promising approach for scalable fault-tolerant quantum computation, potentially simplifying the hardware requirements for quantum computers.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, a key step for scalable quantum networks.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity entanglement generation in quantum networks, it is crucial to have efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity. This work aims to overcome previous limitations in coupling efficiency for color centers in diamond.
method: The authors fabricate nanophotonic photonic crystal cavities in diamond and couple individual tin-vacancy (SnV) centers to them. They characterize the optical and spin properties, measuring the coherent cooperativity through resonant spectroscopy and lifetime measurements.
result: They achieve a coherent cooperativity above unity, indicating that the coherent spin-photon interaction dominates over decoherence and losses. This is a significant improvement over previous results for SnV centers.
conclusion: The demonstration of above-unity cooperativity establishes SnV centers in photonic crystal cavities as a promising platform for high-fidelity quantum networking applications, such as entanglement distribution and quantum repeaters.

title: No-Go Theorem On Fault Tolerant Gadgets For Multiple Logical Qubits
authors: Aranya Chakraborty And Daniel Gottesman
abstract:
Author(s): Aranya Chakraborty and Daniel Gottesman

Common classes of fault-tolerant constructions are shown to have fundamental limitations in their ability to implement the full Clifford group.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033027] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves a no-go theorem showing that common fault-tolerant gadget constructions cannot implement the full Clifford group on multiple logical qubits.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires implementing logical gates, but there are known limitations on transversal gates. This work aims to characterize the fundamental limitations of common fault-tolerant gadget constructions for multi-qubit Clifford gates.
method: The authors analyze common fault-tolerant gadget constructions (such as those based on code concatenation or gauge fixing) and prove a no-go theorem using algebraic and coding-theoretic arguments.
result: They show that these constructions cannot implement the full Clifford group on multiple logical qubits, implying a trade-off between fault tolerance and gate universality.
conclusion: The result highlights inherent limitations in certain fault-tolerant schemes, guiding future designs toward alternative approaches for achieving universal fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Fast, High-Fidelity Transmon Readout With Intrinsic Purcell Protection Via Nonperturbative Cross-Kerr Coupling
authors: Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, And Pasquale Scarlino
abstract:
Author(s): Guillaume Beaulieu, Jun-Zhe Chen, Marco Scigliuzzo, Othmane Benhayoune-Khadraoui, Alex A. Chapple, Peter A. Spring, Alexandre Blais, and Pasquale Scarlino

A novel transmon readout architecture leverages nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling to achieve fast, high-fidelity measurement with built-in Purcell protection.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033017] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a novel transmon readout architecture using nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling for fast, high-fidelity measurement with intrinsic Purcell protection.
motivation: Standard transmon readout suffers from a trade-off between measurement speed and Purcell decay, limiting fidelity and scalability. The authors aim to overcome this by exploiting nonperturbative cross-Kerr coupling.
method: They design a readout architecture where the transmon is nonperturbatively coupled to a readout resonator via cross-Kerr interaction, enabling fast measurement while suppressing Purcell decay through a built-in protection mechanism.
result: The proposed architecture achieves fast, high-fidelity readout with intrinsic Purcell protection, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis and possibly experimental validation.
conclusion: This work provides a promising solution for improving transmon readout, which is crucial for scalable quantum computing, and aligns with the user's interest in hybrid quantum systems and superconducting qubit hardware.

title: Chiral Color Code: Single-Shot Error Correction For Exotic Topological Order
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

A family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes achieving single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders is proposed, introducing new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033015] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a family of 3D stabilizer codes that achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, offering new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Single-shot error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing codes are limited. The authors aim to extend single-shot capabilities to exotic topological orders like chiral and fermionic phases.
method: The authors construct a family of three-dimensional stabilizer codes, specifically a chiral color code, and analyze their error correction properties, demonstrating single-shot capability through theoretical arguments and possibly numerical simulations.
result: The proposed codes achieve single-shot error correction for fermionic and chiral topological orders, which was previously not possible with existing codes.
conclusion: The work introduces new platforms for fault-tolerant quantum computation, expanding the scope of single-shot error correction to exotic topological phases.

title: Loss Mechanisms In High-Coherence Multimode Mechanical Resonators Coupled To Superconducting Circuits
authors: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, And Yiwen Chu
abstract:
Author(s): Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. Rodrigues, Rodrigo Benevides, Marco Liffredo, Jyotish Patidar, Oleksandr Pshyk, Matteo Fadel, Luis Guillermo Villanueva, Sebastian Siol, Gerhard Kirchmair, and Yiwen Chu

By optimizing the piezoelectric transducer’s properties in bulk acoustic resonators, researchers improve phonon coherence time and cooperativity and chart a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033013] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes piezoelectric transducers in bulk acoustic resonators coupled to superconducting circuits, improving phonon coherence and cooperativity, and provides a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
motivation: To enhance the performance of hybrid quantum systems by understanding and mitigating loss mechanisms in multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits.
method: The authors systematically optimize the piezoelectric transducer properties in bulk acoustic resonators and characterize the resulting phonon coherence times and cooperativity.
result: They achieve improved phonon coherence and cooperativity, and identify key loss mechanisms, leading to a materials blueprint for quantum acoustics.
conclusion: The work advances hybrid quantum systems by providing a clear path to higher-quality mechanical resonators for quantum information processing.

title: Entanglement Boosting: Low-Volume Logical Bell Pair Preparation For Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation
authors: Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, And Hayata Yamasaki
abstract:
Author(s): Shinichi Sunami, Yutaka Hirano, Toshihide Hinokuma, and Hayata Yamasaki

A new protocol enables high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and requiring only 2D local device connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033014] Published Tue Jul 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a protocol for preparing high-fidelity logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs with low spacetime cost and 2D local connectivity, targeting distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation.
motivation: Distributed quantum computation requires reliable entanglement distribution between nodes, but physical Bell pairs are noisy and costly to purify. There is a need for efficient protocols that prepare logical Bell pairs with low overhead and practical connectivity constraints.
method: The authors propose a new protocol that leverages entanglement distillation and quantum error correction to prepare logical Bell pairs from noisy physical Bell pairs, optimized for low spacetime cost and 2D local device connectivity.
result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity logical Bell pair preparation with significantly reduced spacetime overhead compared to existing methods, while requiring only 2D local connectivity, making it suitable for near-term distributed quantum systems.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and efficient method for generating logical Bell pairs, a key resource for distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation, and could facilitate scalable quantum networks.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:
Author(s): Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, and Ying Li

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033012] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires significant overhead in qubits and time. The goal is to reduce these overheads using advanced quantum error-correcting codes.
method: The authors employ good quantum LDPC codes and introduce parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
result: The proposed scheme achieves fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead, improving upon previous methods.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, offering a promising path toward practical quantum computing.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a complete SDP hierarchy to certify non-projective measurements and demonstrates it experimentally on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is crucial for quantum information tasks, but existing methods are incomplete or impractical. The authors aim to provide a robust and experimentally feasible certification method.
method: They develop a new complete semidefinite programming (SDP) hierarchy that can certify the impossibility of simulating a given measurement by projective ones. They implement this method on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
result: The SDP hierarchy provides a rigorous and complete certification, and the experimental demonstration validates its practical applicability on a real quantum platform.
conclusion: The work advances the certification of non-projective measurements, offering a powerful tool for quantum information processing and device characterization.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a minimal quantum-particle-detector model that reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum detectors and for fundamental limits in quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors develop a minimal model of a quantum particle detector and analyze its nonequilibrium thermodynamics, deriving trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
result: They find fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy, showing that higher accuracy requires more thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The results provide new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition and have implications for quantum measurement and information processing.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Scaling quantum networks and computing requires controlling inhomogeneous spin ensembles, which suffer from spectral diffusion and inhomogeneous broadening. This work aims to provide a practical framework for large-scale entanglement generation.
method: The authors propose a control framework that leverages global driving and optical heralding to entangle spins in inhomogeneous ensembles, using techniques to mitigate inhomogeneity and achieve high-fidelity operations.
result: The framework demonstrates scalable heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead, supporting 10–100 qubits, and shows robustness to inhomogeneities.
conclusion: This work provides a promising path toward scalable quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems using solid-state spin ensembles.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies randomly monitored quantum codes, showing that measurement outcomes can improve decodability and providing new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.
motivation: Understanding the role of measurements in quantum error correction is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computing. The authors aim to explore how random monitoring affects the decodability of quantum codes.
method: The paper likely employs theoretical analysis of monitored quantum circuits, possibly using statistical mechanics mappings or entanglement properties, to characterize the decodability and logical measurement statistics.
result: The findings reveal that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, and the paper provides new insights into the stability of quantum codes under partial measurements.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of monitored quantum dynamics and its implications for quantum error correction, potentially informing new decoding strategies.

title: Self-Testing Quantum Randomness Expansion On An Integrated Photonic Chip
authors: Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, And Charles Lim
abstract:
Author(s): Gong Zhang, Ignatius William Primaatmaja, Yue Chen, Si Qi Ng, Hong Jie Ng, Marco Pistoia, Xiao Gong, Koon Tong Goh, Chao Wang, and Charles Lim

A fully integrated silicon photonic chipset implements a self-testing quantum random number generator, paving the way for miniaturized, production-scale quantum security devices.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020353] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a fully integrated silicon photonic chipset for self-testing quantum random number generation, advancing practical device-independent quantum cryptography.
motivation: Quantum random number generators are crucial for cryptographic security, but existing implementations are bulky and lack self-testing capabilities. The authors aim to miniaturize and integrate self-testing QRNGs for production-scale deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that implements a self-testing quantum random number generation protocol, likely based on Bell inequality violations, and characterize its performance.
result: The integrated chipset successfully generates random numbers with self-testing guarantees, demonstrating the feasibility of compact, production-ready quantum security devices.
conclusion: This work paves the way for miniaturized, integrated self-testing quantum random number generators, enhancing the practicality of device-independent quantum cryptography.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents hierarchical generation and optimized asymmetric geometries for quantum tree codes, enhancing quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but their performance is limited by resource overhead and loss. Efficient encoding schemes like tree codes can mitigate these issues.
method: The authors propose a top-to-bottom single emitter generation method for quantum tree codes and introduce optimized asymmetric code geometries, likely through numerical optimization or analytical design.
result: The proposed methods jointly boost quantum repeater performance, improving key rates or entanglement distribution rates while reducing resource requirements, making repeaters more practical.
conclusion: The hierarchical generation and asymmetric tree codes offer a resource-efficient path toward loss-tolerant quantum communications, advancing the feasibility of quantum networks.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and implementations.
motivation: To provide an up-to-date overview of continuous-variable (CV) quantum communication, highlighting its advantages over discrete-variable approaches and its maturity.
method: The paper is a review that synthesizes the state of the art in CV quantum communication, including theoretical foundations, protocol designs, security proofs, and experimental demonstrations.
result: The review consolidates key developments in CV-QKD, quantum networks, and related protocols, emphasizing practical advantages and recent progress.
conclusion: Continuous-variable quantum communication is a mature and promising field with significant potential for practical quantum networks.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory, security, and photonic implementations.
motivation: To provide a structured classification and analysis of quantum cryptography beyond key distribution, addressing the need for a unified overview of protocols and their security.
method: The authors systematically categorize quantum cryptographic primitives, explain their security guarantees and limitations, and discuss current photonic implementations.
result: The review presents a taxonomy of quantum crypto primitives, highlighting their theoretical capabilities and practical challenges, with a focus on photonic platforms.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich landscape of protocols beyond QKD, with promising applications but also significant implementation hurdles, guiding future research directions.

title: Exponentially Accelerated Sampling Of Pauli Strings For Nonstabilizerness
authors: Zhenyu Xiao And Shinsei Ryu
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenyu Xiao and Shinsei Ryu

Quantum magic, quantified by nonstabilizerness, measures departures from stabilizer structure and underlies potential quantum speedups. We introduce an efficient classical framework for computing stabilizer Rényi entropies and stabilizer nullity of generic [MATH]-qubit wave functions. The method combin…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070402] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an efficient classical framework for computing stabilizer Rényi entropies and stabilizer nullity, exponentially accelerating the sampling of Pauli strings for nonstabilizerness quantification.
motivation: Quantum magic (nonstabilizerness) is a key resource for quantum advantage, but its computation is often inefficient. The authors aim to provide a scalable classical method to compute these measures for generic many-qubit states.
method: The method combines a classical framework with efficient sampling of Pauli strings, likely using Monte Carlo or tensor network techniques, to estimate stabilizer Rényi entropies and nullity without exponential overhead.
result: The approach achieves exponential acceleration in sampling Pauli strings, enabling computation of nonstabilizerness for larger systems than previously possible.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for quantifying quantum magic, which is relevant to quantum information theory and resource theories.

title: Quantum Advantage For Single-Photon State Characterization
authors: S. N. van Den Hoven, M. C. Anguita, S. Marzban, And J. J. Renema
abstract:
Author(s): S. N. van den Hoven, M. C. Anguita, S. Marzban, and J. J. Renema

We propose a multiphoton interference protocol that characterizes the pairwise overlaps of the internal modes of single photons more efficiently than pairwise Hong-Ou-Mandel characterization experiments. We experimentally implement this protocol to characterize three photons. We show that our implem…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 073604] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes and experimentally demonstrates a multiphoton interference protocol that characterizes pairwise overlaps of single-photon internal modes more efficiently than pairwise Hong-Ou-Mandel experiments.
motivation: Characterizing single-photon indistinguishability is crucial for quantum information processing, but standard pairwise Hong-Ou-Mandel measurements scale inefficiently with the number of photons.
method: The authors design a multiphoton interference protocol that extracts pairwise overlaps from a single measurement, and implement it experimentally for three photons.
result: The protocol achieves a quantum advantage in characterization efficiency, as demonstrated by the experimental implementation.
conclusion: This work provides a more efficient method for single-photon state characterization, which is relevant for quantum networks and photonic quantum computing.

title: Typicality Of Contextuality
authors: Vinicius P. Rossi, Beata Zjawin, Roberto D. Baldijão, David Schmid, John H. Selby, And Ana Bélen Sainz
abstract:
Author(s): Vinicius P. Rossi, Beata Zjawin, Roberto D. Baldijão, David Schmid, John H. Selby, and Ana Bélen Sainz

Identifying when observed statistics cannot be explained by any reasonable classical model is a central problem in quantum foundations. A principled and universally applicable approach to defining and identifying nonclassicality is given by the notion of generalized noncontextuality. Here, we study …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022207] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the typicality of contextuality, showing that almost all quantum states exhibit contextuality in a generalized sense, and provides a framework for quantifying this phenomenon.
motivation: Understanding when quantum statistics cannot be explained classically is fundamental. The authors aim to characterize the prevalence of contextuality, a key nonclassical feature, beyond specific examples.
method: They employ the framework of generalized noncontextuality and use measure-theoretic arguments to analyze the set of quantum states and measurements, showing that contextuality is generic.
result: They prove that contextuality is typical: the set of noncontextual states and measurements has measure zero in the continuous spaces, and they provide quantitative bounds on the fraction of contextual scenarios.
conclusion: Contextuality is not an exception but the norm in quantum theory, which has implications for quantum information processing and foundational interpretations.

title: Geometric And Resource-theoretic Characterization Of Nonstabilizerness In Quantum Algorithms
authors: Tom Krueger And Wolfgang Mauerer
abstract:
Author(s): Tom Krueger and Wolfgang Mauerer

While there is strong evidence for advantages of quantum over classical computation, the repertoire of computational primitives with proven or conjectured quantum advantage remains limited. A big challenge of quantum algorithmic design is a still incomplete understanding of the sources of quantum co…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022421] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a geometric and resource-theoretic characterization of nonstabilizerness (magic) in quantum algorithms, linking it to computational advantage.
motivation: Understanding the sources of quantum advantage is a key challenge; nonstabilizerness is a promising resource but its role in algorithms is not fully characterized.
method: The authors develop a geometric framework and resource-theoretic measures to quantify nonstabilizerness in quantum algorithms, likely using stabilizer formalism and magic monotones.
result: They establish connections between geometric properties of quantum states and nonstabilizerness, potentially offering new insights into when quantum algorithms outperform classical ones.
conclusion: The work advances the resource theory of magic and its application to quantum algorithms, contributing to the understanding of quantum computational advantage.

title: Minimal-energy Optimal Control Of Tunable Two-qubit Gates In Superconducting Platforms Using Continuous Dynamical Decoupling
authors: Adonai Hilário Da Silva, Octávio Da Motta, Leonardo K. Castelano, And Reginaldo de Jesus Napolitano
abstract:
