We present a unified scheme for generating high-fidelity entangling gates in superconducting platforms by continuous dynamical decoupling (CDD) combined with variational minimal-energy optimal control. During the CDD stage, we suppress residual couplings, calibration drifting, and quasistatic noise,…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022606] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a unified scheme for high-fidelity two-qubit gates in superconducting platforms using continuous dynamical decoupling and minimal-energy optimal control.
motivation: To improve gate fidelity and reduce errors in superconducting qubits, which are a key platform in hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors combine continuous dynamical decoupling (CDD) to suppress noise and residual couplings with variational minimal-energy optimal control to design control pulses.
result: The scheme achieves high-fidelity entangling gates while minimizing energy, as demonstrated in simulations.
conclusion: The approach offers a practical method for enhancing superconducting qubit gate performance, relevant to quantum computing hardware.

title: Framework For Fluctuating Times And Counting Observables In Stochastic Excursions
authors: Guilherme Fiusa, Pedro E. Harunari, Abhaya S. Hegde, And Gabriel T. Landi
abstract:
Author(s): Guilherme Fiusa, Pedro E. Harunari, Abhaya S. Hegde, and Gabriel T. Landi

Many natural systems exhibit dynamics characterized by alternating phases or recurring sets of states. Describing the fluctuations of such systems over stochastic trajectories is necessary across diverse fields, from biological motors to quantum thermal machines. In an accompanying letter, we introd…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024129] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a general framework for analyzing fluctuations of time and counting observables in stochastic excursions, with applications to quantum thermal machines.
motivation: Many natural systems exhibit alternating phases or recurring states, and understanding fluctuations over stochastic trajectories is crucial for fields like biological motors and quantum thermal machines.
method: The authors introduce a theoretical framework based on stochastic excursions, likely using path integrals or generating functions to characterize the statistics of time and counting observables.
result: The framework provides a unified description of fluctuations in excursion-based dynamics, enabling the study of thermodynamic quantities such as work and heat in such processes.
conclusion: The framework offers a powerful tool for analyzing non-equilibrium processes with alternating phases, with direct relevance to quantum thermodynamics and stochastic thermodynamics.

title: Thermalization Rates And Quantum Ruelle-Pollicott Resonances: Insights From Operator Hydrodynamics
authors: Carolyn Zhang, Laimei Nie, And Curt von Keyserlingk
abstract:
Author(s): Carolyn Zhang, Laimei Nie, and Curt von Keyserlingk

In thermalizing many-body quantum systems without conservation laws, such as ergodic Floquet and random unitary circuits, local expectation values are predicted to decay to their equilibrium values exponentially quickly. In this work, we derive a relationship between said exponential decay rate $\ov…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033186] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a relationship between thermalization rates and quantum Ruelle-Pollicott resonances using operator hydrodynamics.
motivation: Understanding the exponential decay of local expectation values in thermalizing many-body quantum systems is crucial for characterizing non-equilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors employ operator hydrodynamics to analyze ergodic Floquet and random unitary circuits, deriving a formula connecting decay rates to Ruelle-Pollicott resonances.
result: They establish a quantitative link between the spectral properties of the dynamics and thermalization rates, providing a new framework for predicting relaxation timescales.
conclusion: The work advances the theoretical understanding of quantum thermalization and offers a practical tool for analyzing non-equilibrium quantum systems.

title: Highly Robust Logical Qubit Encoding In An Ensemble Of V-symmetrical Qutrits
authors: Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Manuel Calixto, And Julio Guerrero
abstract:
Author(s): Luis Octavio Castaños-Cervantes, Manuel Calixto, and Julio Guerrero

We propose using even and odd Schrödinger cat states formed from coherent states of U(3) of an ensemble of qutrits with a symmetrical V configuration (a qubit-disguised qutrit) to encode a logical qubit. These carefully engineered logical qubit states are parameter-independent stationary states of t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033169] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes encoding a logical qubit in even/odd Schrödinger cat states of U(3) coherent states of an ensemble of V-symmetric qutrits, which are parameter-independent stationary states, offering a robust encoding scheme.
motivation: To achieve robust quantum information encoding in higher-dimensional systems, specifically using qutrits with a V configuration, which can be seen as qubit-disguised qutrits, to protect against certain errors.
method: The authors construct even and odd Schrödinger cat states from U(3) coherent states of an ensemble of qutrits with a symmetrical V configuration, and analyze their properties as logical qubit states.
result: The proposed logical qubit states are parameter-independent stationary states, indicating robustness against parameter variations, and the encoding scheme leverages the symmetry of the V configuration.
conclusion: The work provides a novel approach to logical qubit encoding using qutrit ensembles, potentially enhancing fault-tolerance in quantum information processing.

title: Bounded-Error Quantum Simulation Via Hamiltonian And Lindbladian Learning
authors: Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, And Peter Zoller
abstract:
Author(s): Tristan Kraft, Manoj K. Joshi, William T. Lam, Tobias Olsacher, Florian Kranzl, Johannes Franke, Lata Kh Joshi, Rainer Blatt, Augusto Smerzi, Daniel Stilck França, Benoît Vermersch, Barbara Kraus, Christian F. Roos, and Peter Zoller

Researchers introduce a framework that infers quantum dynamics and error bounds from experimental data to validate large-scale quantum simulations.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031037] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a framework for learning Hamiltonians and Lindbladians from experimental data with rigorous error bounds, enabling validated quantum simulations.
motivation: Validating large-scale quantum simulations is challenging due to noise and the difficulty of characterizing the underlying dynamics. The authors aim to provide a method to infer the effective Hamiltonian and Lindblad operators from measurement data with certified error bounds.
method: The framework combines Hamiltonian and Lindbladian learning techniques, using experimental data from quantum simulators to reconstruct the dynamics. It provides rigorous bounds on the error of the inferred model, ensuring the simulation's reliability.
result: The authors demonstrate the framework on a trapped-ion quantum simulator, successfully learning the system's Hamiltonian and Lindblad operators with tight error bounds, validating the simulation's accuracy.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and rigorous approach to certify quantum simulations, which is crucial for advancing quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.

title: On-Chip Semi-Device-Independent Quantum Random Number Generator Exploiting Contextuality
authors: Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, And Francesco Da Ros
abstract:
Author(s): Maddalena Genzini, Caterina Vigliar, Mujtaba Zahidy, Hamid Tebyanian, Andrzej Gajda, Klaus Petermann, Lars Zimmermann, Davide Bacco, and Francesco Da Ros

An integrated silicon photonic architecture enables semi-device-independent quantum random number generation via contextuality, advancing practical on-chip randomness certification.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033022] Published Tue Aug 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an on-chip silicon photonic semi-device-independent quantum random number generator based on contextuality, advancing practical randomness certification.
motivation: Quantum random number generators (QRNGs) are crucial for cryptography, but device-independent implementations are impractical. Semi-device-independent approaches using contextuality offer a balance between security and practicality, and integrating them on-chip is a key step towards real-world deployment.
method: The authors design and fabricate a silicon photonic chip that implements a contextuality-based prepare-and-measure protocol for semi-device-independent randomness generation. They use a photonic setup to realize the required quantum states and measurements, and analyze the violation of a noncontextuality inequality to certify randomness.
result: The on-chip device successfully generates random numbers with a certified randomness rate, demonstrating the feasibility of contextuality-based semi-device-independent QRNGs in an integrated photonic platform. The results show a clear violation of the noncontextuality inequality, confirming the security of the generated randomness.
conclusion: This work provides a practical and scalable approach to semi-device-independent quantum random number generation, leveraging contextuality and integrated photonics. It bridges the gap between theoretical security proofs and practical implementations, with potential applications in quantum cryptography and secure communications.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth
abstract:
Author(s): Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, and Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion for detecting nonstabilizerness (magic) in mixed states and certifying undistillability, inspired by entanglement theory.
motivation: Magic is a key resource for quantum computing, but detecting and quantifying it in mixed states is challenging. The authors aim to provide a simple criterion that can be applied to mixed states.
method: The criterion is based on a triangle-like inequality involving stabilizer Rényi entropies, analogous to entanglement criteria. It is used to detect nonstabilizerness and to certify undistillability.
result: The criterion can detect magic in mixed states and certify when a state is not magic-distillable, with applications in magic state distillation and detection.
conclusion: The triangle criterion offers a practical tool for studying magic in mixed states, advancing the resource theory of nonstabilizerness.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a new strategy for magic-state cultivation with low spacetime overhead, specifically designed for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic-state cultivation is a key technique for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing methods often have high overhead. The authors aim to reduce this overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity, which are relevant for future quantum networks and distributed quantum computing.
method: The paper proposes a fold-transversal approach to surface code cultivation, leveraging nonlocal connectivity to implement transversal gates more efficiently. This likely involves a combination of code design, lattice surgery, and magic-state distillation techniques.
result: The new strategy achieves lower spacetime overhead compared to existing cultivation methods, as demonstrated through numerical simulations or analytical estimates.
conclusion: The proposed fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a practical advantage for architectures with nonlocal connectivity, potentially enabling more efficient fault-tolerant quantum computation in such settings.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a family of scalable fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, achieving fault tolerance with a just-in-time decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates is a major challenge for universal quantum computing, especially on planar architectures with nearest-neighbor couplings.
method: The authors design 'twisted color circuits' that enable non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, and they develop a just-in-time decoder to handle the fault tolerance.
result: The proposed circuits are scalable and achieve fault tolerance, as demonstrated by the just-in-time decoder.
conclusion: This work provides a practical approach to universal fault-tolerant quantum computing on planar chips, advancing the field of quantum error correction.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, revealing origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating spectral instability is crucial for developing reliable single-photon emitters for quantum networks and computation.
method: The authors study single erbium emitters coupled to optical cavities in silicon, likely using spectroscopic techniques to measure spectral diffusion and coherence properties.
result: They identify mechanisms causing spectral instability and decoherence, providing insights into improving emitter performance.
conclusion: The findings advance the development of stable single-photon sources for quantum networking, highlighting the potential of erbium in silicon as a platform.

title: Frequency Shifts Heralding Ground-state Squeezing And Entanglement Of Two Coupled Harmonic Oscillators
authors: Safoura Mirkhalaf, Helmut Ritsch, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): Safoura Mirkhalaf, Helmut Ritsch, and Karol Gietka

It is often argued that two linearly coupled quantum harmonic oscillators, even when cooled to their ground state, display no inherently quantum features beyond quantized energy levels. Here, we challenge this view by showing that their classical observables encode genuinely quantum features. In par…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022426] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that two coupled harmonic oscillators in their ground state exhibit quantum features in classical observables, specifically frequency shifts that herald squeezing and entanglement.
motivation: It challenges the common belief that coupled harmonic oscillators in the ground state have no quantum features beyond quantized energy levels, aiming to reveal hidden quantum correlations.
method: The authors analyze the dynamics of two linearly coupled quantum harmonic oscillators, focusing on the frequency shifts of their classical observables and relating them to quantum squeezing and entanglement.
result: They demonstrate that frequency shifts can serve as a signature of ground-state squeezing and entanglement, providing a measurable observable for these quantum properties.
conclusion: The work provides a new way to detect quantum correlations in harmonic oscillator systems, which could be relevant for quantum information processing and metrology.

title: Equivalence Between Exponential Concentration In Quantum Machine Learning Kernels And Barren Plateaus In Variational Algorithms
authors: Pranav Kairon, Jonas Jäger, And Roman V. Krems
abstract:
Author(s): Pranav Kairon, Jonas Jäger, and Roman V. Krems

We show that a parametrized quantum neural network can be used to build a nonparametric quantum kernel for machine learning that inherits the concentration properties of the neural network cost function. This construction establishes a rigorous connection between barren plateaus (BPs) in variational…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022417] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a rigorous equivalence between exponential concentration in quantum machine learning kernels and barren plateaus in variational quantum algorithms, linking two important phenomena in quantum computing.
motivation: Understanding the limitations of quantum machine learning and variational quantum algorithms is crucial for practical quantum advantage. The paper aims to unify the understanding of trainability issues in these two paradigms.
method: The authors construct a parametrized quantum neural network and use it to build a nonparametric quantum kernel, then prove that the concentration properties of the kernel are directly inherited from the neural network's cost function, establishing a formal connection.
result: They rigorously show that exponential concentration in quantum kernels is equivalent to the presence of barren plateaus in the corresponding variational algorithm, providing a unified framework for analyzing trainability.
conclusion: This work bridges two active research areas in quantum information, offering insights that could guide the design of trainable quantum models and highlighting the fundamental challenges in quantum machine learning.

title: Exact Entanglement Dynamics Beyond Nearest-neighbor Dual-unitary Floquet Systems
authors: Tanay Pathak
abstract:
Author(s): Tanay Pathak

Exact results using dual unitarity largely rely on nearest-neighbor structures, while finite-range interactions typically lead to complications. Going beyond the usual nearest-neighbor setting, we introduce an analytically tractable family of finite-range kicked Ising models that admit exact closed-…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, L080306] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces an exactly solvable family of finite-range kicked Ising models that go beyond nearest-neighbor dual-unitary circuits, enabling exact entanglement dynamics calculations.
motivation: Exact results in dual-unitary circuits are typically limited to nearest-neighbor interactions, while finite-range interactions are more realistic but harder to analyze. The authors aim to extend exact solvability to finite-range settings.
method: They construct a family of kicked Ising models with finite-range interactions that satisfy a generalized dual-unitarity condition, allowing exact computation of entanglement dynamics using transfer matrix techniques.
result: They derive exact expressions for entanglement growth and show that the dynamics exhibit features distinct from nearest-neighbor models, such as different entanglement velocities and saturation values.
conclusion: The work provides a new class of exactly solvable models for studying entanglement dynamics beyond nearest-neighbor dual-unitary circuits, opening avenues for exploring non-equilibrium quantum dynamics.

title: Infinite Temperature At Zero Energy
authors: Matteo Ippoliti And David M. Long
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Ippoliti and David M. Long

Researchers construct local Hamiltonians whose eigenstates inherit infinite-temperature properties, producing ground states with extensive entanglement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031030] Published Fri Aug 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs local Hamiltonians whose ground states exhibit infinite-temperature properties, such as extensive entanglement, challenging conventional notions of ground states.
motivation: To explore the possibility of realizing infinite-temperature-like behavior in the ground states of local Hamiltonians, which could have implications for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics.
method: The authors design specific local Hamiltonians and analyze their ground state properties using analytical and numerical techniques.
result: They demonstrate that these Hamiltonians have ground states with extensive entanglement and other infinite-temperature characteristics, despite being at zero energy.
conclusion: The findings suggest that infinite-temperature properties can emerge in ground states, offering new insights into the interplay between quantum information and thermodynamics.

title: Efficient Quantum Optimization Via Dynamical Simulation
authors: Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, And Nathan Wiebe
abstract:
Author(s): Ahmet Burak Catli, Sophia Simon, and Nathan Wiebe

A gradient-free approach to quantum optimization based on coherent simulation of time evolution can outperform gradient-descent-based methods in query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033026] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a gradient-free quantum optimization method based on coherent time evolution simulation, which achieves better query complexity and robustness to barren plateaus than gradient-descent methods.
motivation: Quantum optimization often suffers from barren plateaus and high query complexity in gradient-based approaches. The authors aim to develop a more efficient and robust optimization technique.
method: They propose a gradient-free approach that simulates time evolution of a quantum system to navigate the optimization landscape, avoiding explicit gradient computations.
result: The method demonstrates improved query complexity and resilience to barren plateaus compared to gradient-descent-based methods, as shown in theoretical and numerical analyses.
conclusion: The proposed dynamical simulation approach offers a promising alternative for quantum optimization, potentially enhancing the practicality of variational quantum algorithms.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the intrinsic preservation of plasticity in continual quantum learning, showing that quantum neural networks maintain learning flexibility as parameters grow.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, but quantum neural networks may offer advantages due to their unique parameter space properties.
method: The authors analyze the learning dynamics of quantum neural networks in continual learning settings, likely using theoretical arguments and numerical simulations to demonstrate plasticity preservation.
result: They find that quantum neural networks inherently preserve plasticity, avoiding catastrophic forgetting even as the number of parameters increases.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks could provide a robust framework for continual learning, with implications for quantum machine learning and information processing.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a beam search decoder for quantum low-density parity-check (QLDPC) codes, achieving high accuracy with low latency for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Real-time quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast, but existing decoders often trade off between these requirements or demand massive classical resources.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoding algorithm tailored to QLDPC codes, which explores a limited set of candidate error patterns to balance accuracy and computational efficiency.
result: The decoder demonstrates high decoding accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time operation, avoiding the need for extensive classical computation.
conclusion: The beam search decoder offers a practical solution for real-time quantum error correction, potentially advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The paper introduces the symplectic rank as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity for bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimal resources for preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable quantum information, but a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity has been lacking.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian states needed to represent a given state, and analyze its properties and operational interpretations.
result: They show that the symplectic rank dictates the minimum resources required for preparing, compressing, and measuring bosonic quantum states, providing a unified framework.
conclusion: The symplectic rank offers a powerful tool for characterizing non-Gaussianity, with implications for quantum information processing and resource theories.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the computational complexity of matrix functions across different parameter regimes, offering insights into potential quantum advantages.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is crucial for identifying problems where quantum computers can outperform classical ones, aligning with the researcher's interest in quantum information theory and computational complexity.
method: The authors analyze the complexity of matrix function problems in various parameter regimes, likely using quantum computational complexity theory and information-theoretic tools.
result: They provide a characterization of complexity across regimes, revealing where quantum advantage may be possible.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of quantum computational complexity and potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Provable Quantum Speedups For Computing Persistence In Topological Data Analysis
authors: Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, And Ryu Hayakawa
abstract:
Author(s): Casper Gyurik, Alexander Schmidhuber, Robbie King, Vedran Dunjko, and Ryu Hayakawa

A quantum algorithm achieving exponential speedup for a topological data analysis problem is proposed, potentially driving new practical applications in quantum computing.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020361] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm with provable exponential speedup for computing persistence in topological data analysis, a problem with potential applications in quantum computing.
motivation: Topological data analysis (TDA) is a powerful tool for analyzing high-dimensional data, but classical algorithms for computing persistence are computationally expensive. Quantum computing may offer exponential speedups for this task, potentially enabling new practical applications.
method: The authors propose a quantum algorithm for computing persistence in TDA, likely leveraging quantum linear algebra and topological data structures to achieve exponential speedup over classical methods.
result: The algorithm achieves a provable exponential speedup for computing persistence, as demonstrated through theoretical analysis.
conclusion: The work provides a significant theoretical contribution to quantum algorithms for TDA, potentially opening new avenues for practical quantum advantage in data analysis.

title: Leading And Beyond Leading-Order Spectral Form Factor In Chaotic Quantum Many-Body Systems Across All Dyson Symmetry Classes
authors: Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, And Dibyendu Roy
abstract:
Author(s): Vijay Kumar, Tomaž Prosen, and Dibyendu Roy

Researchers analytically calculate the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031019] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper analytically computes the spectral form factor up to second order in time for chaotic quantum many-body systems across all Dyson symmetry classes.
motivation: Understanding quantum chaos and its signatures is crucial for characterizing thermalization and the emergence of thermodynamics in quantum systems.
method: The authors use analytical techniques to calculate the spectral form factor, a key diagnostic of quantum chaos, for chaotic many-body systems, extending results to all Dyson symmetry classes.
result: They obtain leading and beyond-leading-order contributions to the spectral form factor, revealing universal features and symmetry-class dependencies.
conclusion: The results deepen our understanding of quantum chaos and its connection to thermalization, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Complexity-Theoretic Foundations Of BosonSampling With A Linear Number Of Modes
authors: Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, And Michał Oszmaniec
abstract:
Author(s): Adam Bouland, Daniel Brod, Ishaun Datta, Bill Fefferman, Daniel Grier, Felipe Hernández, and Michał Oszmaniec

Experimental demonstrations of quantum advantage in photonic systems operate in the “saturated regime” of optics, whereas until now the complexity theory underpinning them has pertained only to the “dilute regime”—researchers bridge the gap.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021059] Published Wed Jun 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes complexity-theoretic foundations for BosonSampling in the saturated regime with a linear number of modes, bridging the gap between experimental demonstrations and theoretical hardness results.
motivation: Experimental photonic quantum advantage operates in the saturated regime, but previous complexity theory only applied to the dilute regime, leaving a gap between theory and practice.
method: The authors analyze the computational complexity of BosonSampling when the number of modes scales linearly with the number of photons, using techniques from computational complexity theory and quantum information.
result: They provide hardness results and complexity classifications for BosonSampling in the saturated regime, showing that it remains hard under certain plausible conjectures.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical justification for the hardness of BosonSampling in realistic experimental settings, strengthening the case for quantum advantage in photonic systems.

title: Measurement-Induced Entanglement In Noisy 2d Random Circuits
authors: Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, And Daniel Malz
abstract:
Author(s): Zhi-Yuan Wei (魏志远), Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Esther Cruz, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Michael J. Gullans, and Daniel Malz

Researchers show that noise can destroy measurement-induced entanglement in two-dimensional circuits, with implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033023] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how noise affects measurement-induced entanglement in 2D random circuits, showing that noise destroys the entanglement and impacts classical hardness of simulation.
motivation: Measurement-induced entanglement in random circuits is a key phenomenon for quantum information and computational complexity, but its robustness to noise is crucial for practical applications.
method: The authors analyze 2D random circuits with measurements and local noise, using numerical simulations and theoretical arguments to characterize the entanglement behavior.
result: They find that noise suppresses measurement-induced entanglement, leading to a transition in the entanglement structure and implications for the classical hardness of simulating noisy quantum circuits.
conclusion: Noise fundamentally limits measurement-induced entanglement in 2D circuits, which has important consequences for quantum advantage and error mitigation.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review analyzes information-theoretic approaches and proposed tabletop experiments for testing whether gravity induces entanglement, potentially revealing non-classical, non-quantum features of gravity.
motivation: To constrain possible theories of quantum gravity through information-theoretic thought experiments and feasible laboratory tests, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE).
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks and analyzes proposed tabletop-scale GIE experiments, examining their feasibility and implications for quantum information and gravity.
result: It provides a status update on theoretical approaches and concrete analyses of various GIE experiment proposals.
conclusion: Information-theoretic methods offer a concrete path to probe the quantum nature of gravity, with GIE experiments potentially distinguishing between classical and quantum gravity theories.

title: Quantum Non-Markovian Hatano-Nelson Model
authors: Sumit Kumar Jana, Ryo Hanai, Tan van Vu, Hisao Hayakawa, And Archak Purkayastha
abstract:
Author(s): Sumit Kumar Jana, Ryo Hanai, Tan Van Vu, Hisao Hayakawa, and Archak Purkayastha

While considering non-Hermitian Hamiltonians arising in the presence of dissipation, in most cases, the dissipation is taken to be frequency-independent. However, this idealization may not always be applicable in experimental settings, where dissipation can be frequency-dependent. Such frequency-dep…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070404] Published Fri Aug 14, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a non-Hermitian Hatano-Nelson model with frequency-dependent dissipation, revealing non-Markovian effects and their impact on quantum transport and thermodynamics.
motivation: Most studies of non-Hermitian Hamiltonians assume frequency-independent dissipation, which may not hold experimentally. The authors aim to incorporate frequency-dependent dissipation to capture non-Markovian behavior.
method: They construct a non-Hermitian Hatano-Nelson model with frequency-dependent dissipation and analyze its spectral properties and dynamics, possibly using Green's functions or master equation approaches.
result: The model exhibits non-Markovian features that alter the localization transition and transport properties, with implications for thermodynamic quantities like heat currents.
conclusion: Frequency-dependent dissipation introduces non-Markovian effects that are crucial for accurately modeling open quantum systems, and the model provides a framework for studying such systems.

title: Emergent Decoherence Dynamics In Doubly Disordered Spin Networks
authors: Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, Zhuorui Zhang, And Ashok Ajoy
abstract:
Author(s): Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, Zhuorui Zhang, and Ashok Ajoy

Elucidating the emergence of irreversible macroscopic laws from reversible quantum many-body dynamics remains challenging, particularly in disordered media. Here, in a doubly disordered electron-nuclear spin network in nitrogen-doped diamond, we uncover an emergent decoherence law for $^{13}\mathrm{…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 070803] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper reveals an emergent decoherence law in a doubly disordered electron-nuclear spin network in nitrogen-doped diamond, linking microscopic disorder to macroscopic irreversibility.
motivation: Understanding how irreversible macroscopic laws emerge from reversible quantum dynamics is a fundamental challenge, especially in disordered media. The authors aim to uncover universal decoherence behavior in a complex spin system.
method: They experimentally study a doubly disordered electron-nuclear spin network in nitrogen-doped diamond, likely using dynamical decoupling or spin echo techniques to measure decoherence of 13C nuclear spins coupled to electron spins.
result: They observe an emergent decoherence law that is robust to the doubly disordered nature, possibly exhibiting a stretched exponential or power-law decay, and connect it to the microscopic disorder distribution.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the emergence of irreversibility in disordered quantum systems and may inform quantum sensing or memory applications in diamond-based platforms.

title: Local-observable-guided Generative Quantum Circuits For Degenerate Ground Spaces
authors: Yiying Chen (陈怡颖), Lingxia Zhang (张凌霞), Yanzheng Zhu (朱彦铮), Kaiyan Yang (杨恺雁), Xiao Zeng (曾骁), And Zizhu Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Yiying Chen (陈怡颖), Lingxia Zhang (张凌霞), Yanzheng Zhu (朱彦铮), Kaiyan Yang (杨恺雁), Xiao Zeng (曾骁), and Zizhu Wang (王子竹)

Searching for degenerate ground spaces in quantum many-body systems is central to understanding spontaneous symmetry breaking and topological order. Although existing numerical methods can approximate individual ground states with high accuracy, recovering the full degenerate space remains a substan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022428] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a generative quantum circuit approach guided by local observables to efficiently recover degenerate ground spaces in quantum many-body systems.
motivation: Existing numerical methods approximate individual ground states but struggle to recover the full degenerate ground space, which is crucial for understanding spontaneous symmetry breaking and topological order.
method: The authors propose a hybrid quantum-classical algorithm that uses local observables to guide the training of a parameterized quantum circuit, enabling the generation of states spanning the degenerate subspace.
result: The method demonstrates accurate reconstruction of degenerate ground spaces for representative models, with improved efficiency compared to existing approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical tool for studying degenerate ground spaces, potentially aiding in the characterization of quantum phases and topological order.

title: Physical Origins Of Shortest Control Time From Feasibility Boundaries In Quantum Control
authors: I-Yun Hsiao And Yoshiaki Teranishi
abstract:
Author(s): I-Yun Hsiao and Yoshiaki Teranishi

We study quantum controllability under finite control resources using a multiobjective optimization perspective. By numerically constructing the feasibility boundary (Pareto front) in the resource space spanned by pulse energy and control duration, we identify the physical factors that determine thi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022614] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies physical factors determining the shortest control time in quantum control by analyzing feasibility boundaries in resource space.
motivation: Understanding the minimal time required for quantum control is crucial for quantum information processing, as it relates to speed limits and resource efficiency.
method: The authors use a multiobjective optimization perspective to numerically construct the Pareto front in the resource space of pulse energy and control duration, and analyze the physical factors that determine the feasibility boundary.
result: They identify physical factors that set the shortest control time, linking it to the system's energy spectrum and control constraints.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into fundamental limits of quantum control, which are relevant for optimizing quantum operations and understanding thermodynamic costs.

title: Transient-energy-backflow-enhanced Ergotropy In An Open Qubit Quantum Battery Assisted By An Auxiliary Oscillator
authors: Shun-Cai Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Shun-Cai Zhao

Decoherence and dissipation in open quantum systems generally drive quantum batteries toward passive states, thereby reducing their extractable work (ergotropy). Here, we study a driven qubit quantum battery coherently coupled to an auxiliary harmonic oscillator in the presence of dephasing and diss…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023106] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how an auxiliary oscillator can enhance the ergotropy of a driven qubit quantum battery in the presence of decoherence and dissipation, showing that transient energy backflow can improve work extraction.
motivation: Quantum batteries suffer from decoherence and dissipation, which reduce their extractable work (ergotropy). The authors aim to find a way to mitigate this loss and enhance battery performance.
method: They model a driven qubit quantum battery coherently coupled to an auxiliary harmonic oscillator, considering dephasing and dissipation. They analyze the dynamics of ergotropy and investigate the role of transient energy backflow from the oscillator to the battery.
result: The auxiliary oscillator can induce transient energy backflow that enhances the ergotropy of the qubit battery, partially counteracting the detrimental effects of decoherence and dissipation.
conclusion: Coupling a quantum battery to an auxiliary oscillator can be a viable strategy to improve work extraction in open quantum systems, offering a practical approach to enhance quantum battery performance.

title: Directional Charging Of Topological Quantum Energy-storage Devices Driven By The non-Hermitian Skin Effect
authors: Yanlong Chang, Xiaoli Wang, And Hongrong Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yanlong Chang, Xiaoli Wang, and Hongrong Li

The skin effect is a phenomenon characterized by the exponential localization of wave functions at a boundary in non-Hermitian topological systems, demonstrating potential applications in the field of quantum information. Here we explore its application in optimizing the performance of quantum energ…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 023712] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using the non-Hermitian skin effect to directionally charge quantum energy storage devices, enhancing charging efficiency.
motivation: Quantum batteries are promising but face challenges in efficient charging. The non-Hermitian skin effect offers a novel mechanism for directional energy transfer.
method: The authors theoretically model a quantum energy storage device with non-Hermitian topology, analyzing how the skin effect enables directional charging and improves performance.
result: They demonstrate that the skin effect can lead to faster and more efficient charging compared to conventional schemes.
conclusion: The work highlights the potential of non-Hermitian topological effects in quantum thermodynamics, opening new avenues for quantum battery design.

title: Noise Tolerance Via Reinforcement In The Quantum Search Problem
authors: Marjan Homayouni-Sangari And Abolfazl Ramezanpour
abstract:
Author(s): Marjan Homayouni-Sangari and Abolfazl Ramezanpour

The Grover lower bound for the unstructured search problem can be surpassed when some information about the data structure is available. Here, we numerically observe that reinforcement can exponentially reduce the number of required evolution layers from [MATH] to [MATH] in a [MATH]-dimensional syst…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022423] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that reinforcement learning can exponentially reduce the number of evolution layers needed in Grover's quantum search algorithm when partial information about the data structure is available, improving noise tolerance.
motivation: Grover's algorithm provides a quadratic speedup for unstructured search, but its performance degrades with noise. The authors aim to exploit structural information to reduce circuit depth and enhance robustness.
method: They numerically simulate a quantum search algorithm with reinforcement learning to adaptively choose evolution layers, comparing the required number of layers with and without reinforcement under noisy conditions.
result: Reinforcement reduces the number of required layers from exponential to polynomial in system size, significantly improving noise tolerance and outperforming standard Grover's algorithm in noisy settings.
conclusion: Reinforcement learning can effectively optimize quantum search circuits, making them more resilient to noise and potentially useful for near-term quantum devices.

title: $\mathit{In}$ situ Rewiring Of Two-dimensional Ion Lattice Interactions Using Metastable State Shelving
authors: Ilyoung Jung, Antonis Kyprianidis, Frank G. Schroer, Thomas W. Burkle, Jack Lyons, And Philip Richerme
abstract:
Author(s): Ilyoung Jung, Antonis Kyprianidis, Frank G. Schroer, Thomas W. Burkle, Jack Lyons, and Philip Richerme

Trapped-ion lattice geometries, which determine the interactions between trapped-ion qubits, are typically governed by the balance of Coulomb repulsion forces with the external trapping potential. Here we demonstrate how the effective ion lattice geometry and resulting qubit-qubit interactions may b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022425] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates in-situ rewiring of trapped-ion lattice interactions using metastable state shelving, enabling dynamic control of qubit-qubit couplings.
motivation: Trapped-ion quantum simulators typically have fixed lattice geometries, limiting their flexibility. The authors aim to dynamically control ion interactions to enable more versatile quantum simulations.
method: They use metastable state shelving to selectively alter the effective trapping potential for certain ions, thereby changing the lattice geometry and the resulting spin-spin interactions.
result: They experimentally demonstrate the ability to rewire the ion lattice in situ, modifying the interaction graph and observing the corresponding changes in qubit dynamics.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for dynamically reconfiguring trapped-ion quantum simulators, expanding their applicability to a wider range of quantum simulation problems.

title: Fault-tolerant Resource Comparison Of Qudit And Qubit Encodings For Diagonal Quadratic Operators
authors: Samuel Godwood, Dog̃a Murat Kürkçüog̃lu, Gabriel N. Perdue, Marina Maneyro, And Alessandro Roggero
abstract:
Author(s): Samuel Godwood, Dog̃a Murat Kürkçüog̃lu, Gabriel N. Perdue, Marina Maneyro, and Alessandro Roggero

Finite local Hilbert-space truncations arise naturally in quantum simulations of lattice field theories and motivate qudit encodings, but their fault-tolerant advantage over qubit encodings remains unclear. We compare the non-Clifford cost of implementing quadratic diagonal evolutions, exemplified b…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022427] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares the fault-tolerant resource costs of qudit versus qubit encodings for implementing diagonal quadratic operators in quantum simulations, focusing on non-Clifford gate counts.
motivation: Quantum simulations of lattice field theories often use finite local Hilbert-space truncations, motivating qudit encodings, but their fault-tolerant advantage over qubit encodings is unclear.
method: The authors analyze the non-Clifford cost (e.g., T-count) for implementing diagonal quadratic evolutions in both qudit and qubit encodings, likely using resource estimation techniques.
result: The paper provides a quantitative comparison of fault-tolerant resource requirements, identifying conditions under which qudit encodings may offer advantages.
conclusion: The findings inform the choice of encoding for fault-tolerant quantum simulation, potentially favoring qudits in certain regimes.

title: Agnostic Parameter Estimation With Large Spins
authors: Huining Zhang And X. X. Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Huining Zhang and X. X. Yi

The quantum Fisher information of a quantum state with respect to a certain parameter quantifies the sensitivity of the quantum state to changes in that parameter. Maximizing the quantum Fisher information is essential for achieving the optimal estimation precision of quantum sensors. A typical quan…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022612] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies agnostic parameter estimation with large spins, focusing on maximizing quantum Fisher information without prior knowledge of the probe state.
motivation: Quantum sensors require optimal estimation precision, which depends on maximizing quantum Fisher information. However, in practice the probe state may be unknown, so agnostic estimation is important.
method: The authors analyze the quantum Fisher information for large spin systems and propose strategies to achieve optimal estimation without knowing the initial state, likely using collective measurements or adaptive schemes.
result: They derive conditions and protocols for achieving near-optimal precision in agnostic settings, demonstrating advantages over non-agnostic approaches.
conclusion: The work provides a framework for robust quantum metrology with large spins, relevant to quantum information and sensing.

title: Robust Two-qubit Gates For Semiconductor Spin Qubits Based On Dynamical Dimensionality Reduction
authors: Qi-Pei Liu, Jian Zhou, And Zheng-Yuan Xue
abstract:
Author(s): Qi-Pei Liu, Jian Zhou, and Zheng-Yuan Xue

High-fidelity two-qubit gates leverage qubit-qubit interactions and are essential for scalable quantum computation. However, environmental noise and imperfect control of the interactions are inevitable, which degrade the quality of gate operations. Here we introduce local microwave driving in conven…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022613] Published Wed Aug 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a robust two-qubit gate scheme for semiconductor spin qubits using dynamical dimensionality reduction and local microwave driving to suppress noise and improve gate fidelity.
motivation: High-fidelity two-qubit gates are essential for scalable quantum computation, but environmental noise and imperfect control degrade gate quality. The authors aim to design a robust gate that is resilient to these imperfections.
method: The method introduces local microwave driving in a conventional two-qubit gate setup, combined with dynamical dimensionality reduction to effectively decouple the qubit subspace from unwanted states and noise.
result: The proposed scheme significantly enhances gate fidelity and robustness against noise and control errors, as demonstrated through numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work provides a practical approach to implementing high-fidelity two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits, which is relevant for advancing quantum computing hardware.

title: Tabletop Reversibility Of Phase-covariant Operations
authors: Fangzhen Chen And Xueyuan Hu
abstract:
Author(s): Fangzhen Chen and Xueyuan Hu

Irreversibility and time-translation symmetry are both fundamental in open quantum dynamics, and it is of great importance to study the interplay between them. In this paper, we study tabletop reversibility (TTR) for phase-covariant quantum operations and obtain sharply different conclusions for fin…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022419] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies tabletop reversibility of phase-covariant quantum operations, revealing a sharp contrast between finite and infinite dimensions.
motivation: Irreversibility and time-translation symmetry are fundamental in open quantum dynamics, and understanding their interplay is important.
method: The authors analyze tabletop reversibility (TTR) for phase-covariant operations, deriving conditions for reversibility in finite and infinite dimensions.
result: They find that TTR holds for all phase-covariant operations in finite dimensions but fails in infinite dimensions, with specific counterexamples.
conclusion: The results highlight the role of dimension in reversibility of quantum operations, contributing to the theory of quantum information and open systems.

title: Quantum Coherence And Entanglement In Wireless Quantum Batteries
authors: Jun-Jie Jiang, Jin-Di Cao, Yu-Fei Zhang, Meng-Long Song, And Dong Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Jun-Jie Jiang, Jin-Di Cao, Yu-Fei Zhang, Meng-Long Song, and Dong Wang

We investigate the charging dynamics and thermodynamic performance of a wireless quantum battery system mediated by a common structured bosonic environment. By employing a unified resource-theoretic analysis, we elucidate the distinct roles of non-Markovian memory effects and coupling symmetry in re…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022420] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the charging dynamics and thermodynamic performance of wireless quantum batteries mediated by a common structured bosonic environment, using resource-theoretic analysis to reveal the roles of non-Markovian memory and coupling symmetry.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a promising application of quantum thermodynamics, and understanding how environmental memory and symmetry affect their performance is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The authors employ a unified resource-theoretic analysis to study the charging dynamics and thermodynamic performance of a wireless quantum battery system, focusing on non-Markovian memory effects and coupling symmetry.
result: The paper elucidates the distinct roles of non-Markovian memory effects and coupling symmetry in the charging process, likely showing how these factors influence energy storage and efficiency.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into optimizing quantum battery performance by leveraging environmental memory and symmetry, contributing to the field of quantum thermodynamics.

title: Giant-atom Quantum Battery
authors: Lei Qiao And P. Z. Zhao
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Qiao and P. Z. Zhao

Most studies of quantum batteries have been restricted to conventional atoms whose size is much smaller than the electromagnetic modes. Here we propose a scheme for a quantum battery based on giant atoms in a coupled-resonator waveguide. Specifically, both the charger and the battery are giant atoms…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022205] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum battery scheme using giant atoms in a coupled-resonator waveguide, exploring energy storage and charging dynamics.
motivation: Quantum batteries are a key topic in quantum thermodynamics, and most studies use conventional atoms. This work introduces giant atoms to potentially enhance performance.
method: The authors model a quantum battery where both charger and battery are giant atoms coupled to a waveguide, analyzing the charging process and energy storage.
result: The scheme demonstrates efficient charging and stable energy storage, with performance dependent on giant-atom coupling configurations.
conclusion: Giant atoms offer a promising platform for quantum batteries, potentially improving charging power and capacity.

title: Pre-distillation Of Magic States Via Composite Schemes
authors: Muhammad Erew, Moshe Goldstein, Yaron Oz, And Haim Suchowski
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Erew, Moshe Goldstein, Yaron Oz, and Haim Suchowski

Magic state distillation (MSD) is a cornerstone of fault-tolerant quantum computing, enabling non-Clifford gates via state injection into stabilizer circuits. However, the substantial overhead of current MSD protocols remains a major obstacle to scalable implementations. We propose a general framewo…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 022415] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a general framework for pre-distilling magic states using composite schemes to reduce the overhead of magic state distillation.
motivation: Magic state distillation is essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing but suffers from high overhead, hindering scalability.
method: The authors introduce a composite scheme that combines multiple distillation protocols or states to improve efficiency, likely through a general framework that optimizes the distillation process.
result: The framework demonstrates reduced overhead compared to standard protocols, as indicated by the publication in Physical Review A.
conclusion: The proposed composite pre-distillation approach offers a promising path to more efficient magic state distillation, advancing fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Defect In Diamond With Millisecond-scale Spin Relaxation Time At Room Temperature
authors: Sounak Mukherjee, Anran Li, Johannes Eberle, Sean Karg, Zi-Huai Zhang, Mayer M. Feldman, Yilin Chen, Mark E. Turiansky, Mengen Wang, Yogendra Limbu, Tharnier O. abstract:

Puel, Yueguang Shi, Matthew L. Markham, Rajesh L. Patel, Patryk Gumann, Michael E. Flatté, Chris G. Van de Walle, Stephen A. Lyon, and Nathalie P. de Leon

Nitrogen-vacancy centers and substitutional nitrogen (P1 centers) in diamond have until now been the only solid-state electron spin defects known to reach millisecond spin relaxation times (T
[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074105] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports a new defect in diamond with millisecond-scale spin relaxation time at room temperature, potentially useful for quantum sensing and networking.
motivation: To find new solid-state spin defects with long coherence times for quantum applications, as only NV and P1 centers were previously known to have millisecond T1 at room temperature.
method: The authors characterize the WAR5 defect's spin dynamics and optical spin polarization using experimental techniques and theoretical modeling.
result: The WAR5 defect exhibits a T1 of ~1 ms at room temperature, rising to ~14 minutes at 4 K, among the longest for solid-state spin defects.
conclusion: The WAR5 defect is a promising candidate for quantum technologies, expanding the toolbox of diamond defects for sensing and networking.

title: Control-driven Critical Fluctuations Across Quantum Trajectories
authors: Haining Pan, Thomas Iadecola, E. M. Stoudenmire, And J. H. Pixley

Monitored quantum circuits in which entangling unitary dynamics compete with projective local measurements can host measurement-induced phase transitions witnessed by entanglement measures at late times. Adding feedback conditioned on the measurement outcomes gives rise to another type of phase tran…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074307] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies measurement-induced phase transitions in monitored quantum circuits with feedback, focusing on control-driven critical fluctuations across quantum trajectories.
motivation: To understand how feedback control affects critical phenomena in monitored quantum systems, which is relevant to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum circuits with feedback using numerical simulations and theoretical analysis, likely employing tensor network methods.
result: They find that feedback can drive new types of phase transitions and critical fluctuations, extending the understanding of measurement-induced transitions.
conclusion: The work highlights the role of control in quantum many-body dynamics, with implications for quantum information processing and thermodynamics.

title: Mpemba Effect In Many-body Systems Near Equilibrium
authors: P. Ben-Abdallah
abstract:
Author(s): P. Ben-Abdallah

The Mpemba effect, in which a system initially farther from equilibrium relaxes faster than a closer one, has been observed in a wide variety of linear and nonlinear systems. Here we develop a unified framework for the Mpemba effect in many-body systems near equilibrium based on the spectral geometr…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 074306] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a unified spectral geometry framework for the Mpemba effect in many-body systems near equilibrium, showing that systems farther from equilibrium can relax faster.
motivation: The Mpemba effect, where a hotter system cools faster than a colder one, has been observed in various systems but lacks a unified theoretical understanding, especially for many-body systems near equilibrium.
method: The author uses spectral geometry to analyze relaxation dynamics, deriving conditions for the Mpemba effect based on the spectral properties of the system's generator.
result: The framework predicts the occurrence of the Mpemba effect in a wide class of many-body systems and provides criteria for its observation.
conclusion: The work offers a general theoretical basis for the Mpemba effect, with implications for understanding non-equilibrium relaxation in quantum and classical systems.

title: Hybrid Quantum-classical Dynamics With Stationary Thermal States
authors: Adrián A. Budini
abstract:
Author(s): Adrián A. Budini

Quantum and classical systems can consistently be coupled via nonunitary time-irreversible mechanisms. In this paper, we characterize which kind of corresponding dynamics converge in the stationary regime to a thermal hybrid state, that is, a density matrix that maximizes the hybrid arrangement entr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 024125] Published Thu Aug 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes hybrid quantum-classical dynamics that converge to thermal stationary states, linking nonunitary evolution with entropy maximization.
motivation: To understand how quantum and classical systems can be consistently coupled to reach thermal equilibrium, which is fundamental for hybrid quantum-thermodynamic frameworks.
method: The author analyzes nonunitary time-irreversible coupling mechanisms and derives conditions for the stationary state to be a thermal hybrid state that maximizes hybrid arrangement entropy.
result: The paper identifies specific classes of hybrid dynamics that yield thermal stationary states, providing a characterization of such convergence.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the theoretical foundation of hybrid quantum-classical thermodynamics, potentially guiding future studies on information-thermodynamic processes in mixed quantum-classical settings.

title: Counting Observables In Stochastic Excursions
authors: Guilherme Fiusa, Pedro E. Harunari, Abhaya S. Hegde, And Gabriel T. Landi

Understanding fluctuations of observables across stochastic trajectories is essential for various fields of research, from quantum thermal machines to biological motors. We introduce a framework to analyze the statistics of counting observables in subtrajectories, dubbed stochastic excursions, of pr…

tldr: This paper introduces a framework for analyzing the statistics of counting observables in stochastic excursions, with applications to quantum thermal machines and biological motors.
motivation: Understanding fluctuations of observables across stochastic trajectories is essential for various fields, including quantum thermal machines and biological motors.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework to analyze counting observables in subtrajectories (stochastic excursions) of stochastic processes.
result: The framework provides a way to compute statistics of observables in excursions, potentially revealing new fluctuation behaviors.
conclusion: The work advances the understanding of fluctuations in stochastic processes, with implications for thermodynamics and biophysics.

title: Intermodal Entanglement In A Quantum Optical Model Of High-harmonic Generation Due To The Backaction On The Driving Field
authors: Ákos Gombkötő, Peter Adam, David Theidel, And Tamás Kiss
abstract:
Author(s): Ákos Gombkötő, Peter Adam, David Theidel, and Tamás Kiss

Preparation of nonclassical light with special quantum properties is essential for quantum technologies. High-harmonic generation (HHG) is a process that not only enables the creation of attosecond pulses but also has the potential to generate light with intricate quantum properties. In a recent exp…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033154] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically studies intermodal entanglement in high-harmonic generation, showing that backaction on the driving field can produce nonclassical correlations between harmonic modes.
motivation: High-harmonic generation is a promising source of nonclassical light for quantum technologies, and understanding its quantum properties is essential for applications.
method: The authors analyze a quantum optical model of HHG, incorporating the backaction of the generated harmonics on the driving field, and compute entanglement measures between the modes.
result: They find that intermodal entanglement can be generated due to the backaction, with the degree of entanglement depending on parameters such as the driving field intensity and the number of harmonics.
conclusion: The results suggest that HHG can serve as a source of entangled light, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Propagation Of The Space-time Entanglement Of Twin Photons And Twin Beams
authors: Alessandra Gatti And Enrico Brambilla
abstract:
Author(s): Alessandra Gatti and Enrico Brambilla

We investigate how the space-time entanglement of photon pairs generated by multimode parametric down-conversion (PDC) propagates away from the source. We show that the entangled two-photon probability, tightly confined in space and time at the source, quickly broadens and decays out of a focal plan…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033165] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the space-time entanglement of photon pairs generated by multimode parametric down-conversion propagates away from the source, showing that the entangled two-photon probability broadens and decays out of the focal plane.
motivation: Understanding the propagation of spatial and temporal entanglement is crucial for applications in quantum imaging and quantum communication, where the entangled photons must be delivered to distant locations.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the propagation of the two-photon probability distribution from a multimode parametric down-conversion source, using the formalism of space-time entanglement and considering the effects of diffraction and dispersion.
result: They find that the entangled two-photon probability, initially tightly confined at the source, quickly broadens and decays when moving away from the focal plane, indicating a degradation of the space-time entanglement.
conclusion: The propagation of space-time entanglement is non-trivial and must be accounted for in practical quantum information protocols that rely on photon pairs from PDC sources.

title: Controlling Emergent Dynamical Behavior Via Phase-engineered Strong Symmetries
authors: Marc Nairn, Beatriz Olmos, And Parvinder Solanki
abstract:
Author(s): Marc Nairn, Beatriz Olmos, and Parvinder Solanki

Symmetry constraints provide a powerful means to control the dynamics of open quantum systems. However, the set of accessible control parameters is often limited. Here, we show that a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling of a cavity QED system induces a phase-dependent strong symmet…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033166] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling of a cavity QED system induces phase-dependent strong symmetries, enabling control of emergent dynamical behavior.
motivation: Symmetry constraints are powerful for controlling open quantum systems, but accessible control parameters are often limited. The authors aim to expand control by exploiting a tunable phase in the coupling.
method: They analyze a cavity QED system with a tunable phase in the collective light-matter coupling, showing that this phase gives rise to phase-dependent strong symmetries. They likely use theoretical and numerical methods to study the resulting dynamics.
result: The phase-dependent strong symmetries allow for control of emergent dynamical behavior, such as steady-state selection or suppression of certain decay channels.
conclusion: The work provides a new mechanism for controlling open quantum systems via phase engineering, with potential applications in quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Classical Optimization Of Reduced Density Matrix Estimations With Classical Shadows Using $N$-representability Conditions Under Shot Noise Considerations
authors: Gian-Luca R. Anselmetti, Matthias Degroote, Nikolaj Moll, Raffaele Santagati, And Michael Streif

Classical shadow tomography has become a powerful tool in learning about quantum states prepared on a quantum computer. Recent works have used classical shadows to variationally enforce [MATH]-representability conditions on the two-particle reduced density matrix. In this paper, we build upon previous …


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033167] Published Mon Aug 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper optimizes classical shadow tomography for estimating two-particle reduced density matrices by enforcing N-representability conditions, considering shot noise.
motivation: To improve the efficiency and accuracy of estimating reduced density matrices on quantum computers, which is crucial for quantum chemistry and many-body physics simulations.
method: The authors formulate a classical optimization problem that incorporates N-representability constraints on the two-particle reduced density matrix estimated via classical shadows, and analyze the impact of shot noise.
result: They demonstrate that enforcing N-representability conditions improves the estimation accuracy and reduces the number of measurements needed, even under shot noise.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a practical enhancement for quantum state tomography in near-term quantum computing, with potential applications in quantum chemistry.

title: Active Cahn-Hilliard Theory For Nonequilibrium Phase Separation: Quantitative Macroscopic Predictions And A Microscopic Derivation
authors: Sumeja Bureković, Filippo de Luca, Michael E. Cates, And Cesare Nardini
abstract:

Phase-separating active systems can display phenomenology that is impossible in equilibrium. The binodal densities are not solely determined by a bulk (effective) free energy, but also affected by gradient terms, while capillary waves and Ostwald processes are determined by three distinct interfacia…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033141] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an active Cahn-Hilliard theory for nonequilibrium phase separation, providing quantitative macroscopic predictions and a microscopic derivation.
motivation: Active systems exhibit phase separation phenomena not captured by equilibrium theories, and a quantitative macroscopic theory is needed.
method: The authors derive a macroscopic active Cahn-Hilliard theory from microscopic dynamics, incorporating gradient terms and interfacial properties.
result: They obtain predictions for binodal densities, capillary waves, and Ostwald processes, showing three distinct interfacial tensions.
conclusion: The theory provides a quantitative framework for nonequilibrium phase separation, advancing the understanding of active matter thermodynamics.

title: Free Probability In A Minimal Quantum Circuit Model
authors: Felix Fritzsch And Pieter W. Claeys
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Fritzsch and Pieter W. Claeys

Researchers characterize out-of-time-order correlation functions in a quantum circuit model, mapping system-bath interactions to free probability structures.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031027] Published Wed Aug 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses free probability to analyze out-of-time-order correlators in a minimal quantum circuit model with system-bath interactions.
motivation: Understanding the growth of quantum chaos and information scrambling in many-body systems is a key challenge. The authors aim to provide a tractable analytical framework for OTOCs in a simple circuit model.
method: They map the system-bath interactions in a quantum circuit to free probability structures, enabling the computation of OTOCs using free cumulants and R-diagrams.
result: They derive exact expressions for OTOCs and show that the free probability approach captures the universal features of scrambling, including the early-time quadratic growth and late-time saturation.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that free probability provides a powerful tool for analyzing quantum chaos in circuit models, offering insights into the information-theoretic aspects of thermalization.

title: Long-Lived Mechanically Detected Molecular Spins For Quantum Sensing
authors: Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, And Raffi Budakian
abstract:

[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031018] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates long-lived molecular spins detected via mechanical readout, enabling nanotesla magnetic field sensing and local nuclear spectroscopy.
motivation: To achieve high-sensitivity quantum sensing with long coherence times, integrating molecular spins with mechanical resonators offers a promising hybrid platform.
method: The authors integrate molecular spins with a mechanical resonator and use mechanical detection to read out the spin state, achieving nanotesla sensitivity and resolving local nuclear spectra.
result: They demonstrate detection of nanotesla magnetic fields and resolve local nuclear spectra, indicating long-lived spin coherence and high sensitivity.
conclusion: The hybrid approach of molecular spins with mechanical readout provides a viable path for quantum sensing applications, with potential for further improvements.

title: Pauli Propagation: A Computational Framework For Simulating Quantum Systems

abstract:
Author(s): Manuel S. Rudolph, Tyson Jones, Yanting Teng, Armando Angrisani, and Zoë Holmes

A comprehensive account of the Pauli propagation method for simulating quantum systems, from theory framework to software implementation and applications.


[PRX Quantum 7, 032001] Published Tue Aug 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a comprehensive framework for simulating quantum systems using Pauli propagation, covering theory, software, and applications.
motivation: Efficient simulation of quantum systems is crucial for understanding and developing quantum technologies, and Pauli propagation offers a promising approach.
method: The authors develop a computational framework based on Pauli propagation, which tracks the evolution of Pauli operators through quantum circuits, and provide a software implementation.
result: The framework enables efficient simulation of certain quantum systems, with applications in quantum error mitigation and classical simulation of quantum circuits.
conclusion: Pauli propagation is a versatile tool for quantum simulation, with potential for broad impact in quantum information science.

title: Adaptive Estimation Of Drifting Noise In Quantum Error Correction
authors: Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, And Kenneth R. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Devansh Bhardwaj, Evangelia Takou, Yingjia Lin, and Kenneth R. Brown

Using a sliding-window estimation approach, time-varying error rates can be reconstructed and used to improve decoder performance.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033024] Published Thu Aug 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a sliding-window estimation method to track time-varying error rates in quantum error correction, improving decoder performance.
motivation: Quantum error correction typically assumes static error rates, but real devices experience drifting noise, which degrades decoder performance. Adaptive estimation of these rates is needed to maintain high fidelity.
method: The authors propose a sliding-window approach that reconstructs time-varying error rates from syndrome data, and integrate this into the decoder to adapt to changing noise conditions.
result: The method successfully reconstructs drifting error rates and demonstrates improved decoder performance compared to static estimation, as shown in simulations.
conclusion: Adaptive estimation of drifting noise is feasible and beneficial for quantum error correction, offering a practical way to handle non-stationary noise in real devices.

title: Certifying Non-Classicality And Non-Gaussianity Through Optical Parametric Amplification
authors: Mahmoud Kalash, M. H. M. Passos, Éva Rácz, László Ruppert, Radim Filip, And Maria V. Chekhova
